evidence: test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py hardcodes comment_limits.truncate_comment_body (Cloud-only module) as the send-path transform at line 154
test_outbound_description_length_convergence.py hardcodes ADF_PATH and _ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32000 (ADF-specific, not a DC concept) at lines 31-34
The DC equivalents differ structurally: DC uses WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound (plain char truncation at WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT=32767), not ADF-based fitting
cedc explicitly provides a fallback ('decide by trying the parametrization first; a split is the fallback, not the default'), but 79d5 provides no such fallback
Absent: any acknowledgment in 79d5 that the existing Cloud convergence suites' internals are Cloud-specific and may prevent direct parametrization
findings.finding: The 79d5 plan says DC convergence tests will be 'parametrized alongside Cloud's where the mechanism is shared,' but the existing Cloud convergence suites are not structured for parametrization — they hardcode Cloud-specific internals (comment_limits.truncate_comment_body, ADF path constants, _ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT) that have no DC equivalents. An implementer following the plan literally would either restructure incident-hardened Cloud tests (introducing blast radius and risk) or discover the parametrization is infeasible and fall back to separate DC files — but the plan names no fallback here, unlike cedc which explicitly says 'split is the fallback, not the default.' Without either a positive rationale for why parametrization is feasible despite these Cloud-specific internals, or an acknowledged fallback, the implementer is left to resolve this tension silently.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before closing `79d5`, add at minimum a constructor/config parameter (or a per-adapter introspection hook) that allows the DC adapter to accept an overridden character limit at instantiation time, so that the hardcoded `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` becomes a *default* rather than an immutable constant — deferring the full admin-configurable story to `049e` while leaving no override path at all means any non-default instance silently misbehaves.
evidence: Plan text: 'the DC comment ceiling's PROVENANCE is cited in the source at the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding — naming `jira.text.field.character.limit` and JRASERVER-28519'
Plan text: 'that it is admin-configurable is tracked separately as `049e-9fac-a821-4ea2` and does NOT gate this epic'

T5e(b): 'Rules/thresholds expected to evolve are configurable, not hardcoded' — the plan explicitly acknowledges this threshold can be changed by an admin yet still hardcodes it without a runtime override path
findings.finding: The plan introduces `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` as a hardcoded constant derived from Jira's `jpm.xml`, explicitly acknowledges that this value is admin-configurable per-instance, and defers the configurable version to a separate ticket (`049e-9fac-a821-4ea2`). T5e(b) requires that thresholds expected to evolve are configurable, not hardcoded. The plan provides no hook, override mechanism, or interface boundary that would allow a Jira DC instance with a non-default character limit to inject its actual limit — the constant will silently truncate at the wrong boundary for any admin who has changed `jira.text.field.character.limit` away from the default.
findings.location: AC `79d5-63c7-5f31-48a7` — `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding and the parenthetical '(The ceiling is no longer unknown … that it is admin-configurable is tracked separately as `049e-9fac-a821-4ea2` and does NOT gate this epic)'
scenarios: A DC admin who has raised `jira.text.field.character.limit` beyond the default will have the adapter truncate comments earlier than necessary, silently discarding content that Jira would have accepted — a data-loss regression invisible in CI because CI uses the default-configured instance.
A DC admin who has lowered the limit below the default will have the adapter submit comments that exceed the real limit, producing Jira API 400 errors at runtime — again invisible in the test suite.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the constant into a default-valued parameter (e.g., `max_comment_chars: int = WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT`) on the DC adapter's constructor or on the length-convergence helper, so the hardcoded value can be overridden without a code change. Document in the source comment (alongside the JRASERVER-28519 citation) that this default is correct for stock instances and that `049e` tracks making it runtime-configurable.

evidence: AC for bd9e: 'exactly ONE dict literal defines the local->Jira ticket-type map within adapters/'
Plan only names 'DC's create path' as the reader: 'bd9e (the duplicated ticket-type map is read by DC's create path)'
ABSENCE: Cloud's create path — which presumably also reads a ticket-type map — is not mentioned as a caller that must be verified to keep the same behavior after the map is consolidated
Scope caveat: 'No behaviour change to either adapter is intended; where a test reveals one is needed, that becomes its own bug ticket rather than being folded in silently'
findings.finding: The bd9e child introduces a production change — consolidating the ticket-type map into a single canonical literal — but the plan only names DC's create path as a reader of that map. It does not acknowledge Cloud's create path (or any other caller) as depending on whichever copy currently 'wins', so callers that may behave differently if the chosen canonical copy differs from what they currently use are not acknowledged.
findings.location: bd9e acceptance criterion; 'Scope' section ('one map is genuinely duplicated and must be single-sourced before it can be guarded')
scenarios: If the two duplicate map literals currently differ (even by one entry), consolidating to one will silently change behavior for whichever adapter was using the 'other' copy. Because Cloud's create path is not named as a caller to verify, that regression could land unnoticed.

The guard test (test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py) only asserts that exactly one copy exists; it does not assert that the surviving copy is value-identical to what Cloud was previously using, so it would pass even if Cloud's ticket-type mapping silently changed.
findings.suggested_fix: Before removing the second literal, assert (in the PR or a test) that both copies are byte-for-byte identical. If they differ, surface the difference as a bug ticket rather than silently picking one. Add this as a sub-step to the bd9e AC: 'Prior to removal, a script or test confirms both literals are identical; any divergence is recorded as a separate defect.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Mark `famous-enslaved-unau` (single-source the ticket-type map) as a hard prerequisite for `brokendown-unfiring-inganue` (DC characterization suite) — either in the child ticket descriptions or in the epic's sequencing note — so no developer can start the characterization suite before the map's canonical location is settled.
evidence: 'bd9e (the duplicated ticket-type map is read by DC's create path)' — plan notes the coupling but does not mark it a hard prerequisite
AC for cedc says 'the shared `map_fields_to_remote` body is exercised through `WikiTextCodec` as well as `AdfCodec`' — this presupposes single-sourcing is complete
Both children are listed as equal 'come first' priority without an ordering constraint between them
ABSENCE: no explicit 'depends on' or 'must be merged before' language linking the two children
findings.finding: The execution-order dependency between `famous-enslaved-unau` (single-source the ticket-type map) and `brokendown-unfiring-inganue` (DC characterization suite) is implied by the priority framing but never made explicit as a blocking prerequisite. Both are listed as 'come first' priority items. If a developer picks up `brokendown-unfiring-inganue` before `famous-enslaved-unau` is merged, they will write characterization tests against a still-duplicated map; when the map is subsequently single-sourced and moved, those tests may need revision or will exercise the wrong import path. The plan notes that 'the shared `map_fields_to_remote` body is exercised through `WikiTextCodec` as well as `AdfCodec`' in cedc's AC, which presupposes the map is already single-sourced.
findings.location: Priority framing section; AC for `cedc-58d1-f6d1-428e`; children `famous-enslaved-unau` and `brokendown-unfiring-inganue`
scenarios: Developer starts `brokendown-unfiring-inganue` while `famous-enslaved-unau` is in review; characterization tests import from one of the two duplicate locations; after single-sourcing the import path changes and the tests silently test nothing or fail to import
Reviewer approves `brokendown-unfiring-inganue` in isolation, not realising the map it exercises will move
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line dependency note to both child tickets: 'Depends on `famous-enslaved-unau` being merged first — the characterization suite must import `map_fields_to_remote` from its final single-sourced location, not from a duplicate that will subsequently be deleted.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] 79d5 AC4 must be tightened: when the ceiling is known (as the parent states it now is), require a source comment at `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` citing `jira.text.field.character.limit` and JRASERVER-28519 — the UNVERIFIED path must not remain a valid closing condition given the parent's assertion that provenance is established.
evidence: Parent AC2: 'the DC comment ceiling's PROVENANCE is cited in the source at the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding — naming `jira.text.field.character.limit` and JRASERVER-28519 — so the constant reads as a decision rather than an assumption. (The ceiling is no longer unknown: it was established from Jira's `jpm.xml`...) Verified by reading the cited comment in the diff'

Child 79d5 AC4: 'the real DC comment ceiling is either MEASURED (with the measurement recorded here) or explicitly marked UNVERIFIED at the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding, so a reader cannot mistake an assumption for a decision'
Child 79d5 AC4 explicitly offers the UNVERIFIED path as a valid completion condition; parent says ceiling is NOW KNOWN and demands a source comment citing both artefacts
No other sibling covers the provenance-in-source-comment requirement
findings.finding: Child 79d5's AC4 allows marking the DC comment ceiling UNVERIFIED as an alternative to measuring it, but the parent AC2 states the ceiling is now known (established from Jira's jpm.xml) and requires the provenance to be CITED IN SOURCE at the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding — specifically naming `jira.text.field.character.limit` and JRASERVER-28519. An implementer following child 79d5's ACs literally could mark the binding UNVERIFIED and close the child ticket while leaving the parent's verifier unsatisfied, because the parent says 'Verified by reading the cited comment in the diff' — a diff artifact that 79d5 does not require.
scenarios: Implementer measures the ceiling, finds it is 32767, records it on the ticket — but does not add the source comment citing JRASERVER-28519 and jira.text.field.character.limit. Child 79d5 closes (MEASURED path satisfied). Parent completion verifier checks for the cited comment in the diff and fails.
Implementer marks binding UNVERIFIED. Child closes. Parent AC2 is unsatisfied because the parent explicitly states the ceiling is no longer unknown.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 79d5 AC4 with: 'the source at `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` carries a comment citing `jira.text.field.character.limit` and JRASERVER-28519, so the constant reads as a decision; if the implementer cannot confirm the citation from jpm.xml during this work, mark UNVERIFIED AND file a linked bug — the UNVERIFIED path does not close the parent criterion.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the cedc/bd9e issuetype ownership gap: either (a) add an explicit dependency in cedc stating it must be implemented after bd9e and should reuse bd9e's issuetype pins rather than authoring new ones, with cedc AC1 listing `issuetype` as 'covered by bd9e' rather than authored here; or (b) narrow bd9e ACs 8-9 to 'Cloud create path only' and confirm cedc owns DC issuetype pins, removing the claimed overlap.
evidence: bd9e scope/testing section: 'Ownership note: sibling story cedc (DC backend characterization suite) also touches DC create-path characterization. To remove the ambiguity, the type-mapping pins are owned here; cedc depends on this ticket and should reuse these pins rather than re-author them.'

cedc AC1: 'the create-path mapper `_map_local_to_dc_fields` is pinned by VALUE for every key it emits — `summary` (from local `title`), `description` (through `WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound`), `issuetype`, `priority`, `status`, `assignee`'
cedc contains no reference to bd9e as a prerequisite or dependency
bd9e AC8: 'the type mapping is pinned by value for the Cloud create path, for all four local types'
bd9e AC9: 'the type mapping is pinned by value for the DC create path, for all four local types'
findings.finding: Both cedc and bd9e plan to pin the issuetype/ticket-type values by value for the DC create path, creating a scope overlap with undefined ownership resolution in cedc. bd9e explicitly claims ownership ('the type-mapping pins are owned here unconditionally') and states 'cedc depends on this ticket and should reuse these pins rather than re-author them.' However, cedc AC1 lists `issuetype` as a field it pins by value ('the create-path mapper `_map_local_to_dc_fields` is pinned by VALUE for every key it emits — `summary`, `description`, `issuetype`, `priority`, `status`, `assignee`') and contains no reference to bd9e as a prerequisite. An implementer reading only cedc would author issuetype pins from scratch, creating duplicate or conflicting assertions when bd9e lands.
findings.location: child cedc-58d1-f6d1-428e AC1 and child bd9e-0740-1b47-47f8 ACs 8-9
scenarios: Implementer picks up cedc first (higher priority per parent's framing: 'DC-DIRECTION GAPS COME FIRST'). They write issuetype pins in test_backend_characterization.py. bd9e is later implemented, also writing issuetype pins. Two sets of issuetype pins exist, potentially with different fixture structures, import paths (pre- vs post-relocation), or assertion styles.

bd9e relocates the map literal. cedc's issuetype pins, written before the relocation, import from the old location (jira_datacenter/backend.py). After bd9e lands, cedc's test still passes (alias preserved) but the two pin sets duplicate each other, causing confusion about which is authoritative.

Implementer of cedc, seeing issuetype in AC1, authors a full table; implementer of bd9e, seeing AC8-9, authors a different full table. Both close their tickets. The duplication is only discovered at parent closeout.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to cedc's scope/context: 'Note: issuetype pins for the DC create path are OWNED by bd9e (ACs 8-9). cedc should import and/or reference those pins rather than re-authoring them. bd9e must be completed before cedc authors its AC1 issuetype assertions.' Alternatively, remove `issuetype` from cedc AC1 and add a cross-reference.

findings.finding: AC4 scope-narrowing in child 79d5: the AC as written permits exactly two resolutions — MEASURED (with the measurement recorded on the ticket) or UNVERIFIED (label applied at the binding) — but the ticket comment establishes a third resolution path that the AC text does not permit: documenting the 32767 ceiling via primary-source provenance (jpm.xml `jira.text.field.character.limit` + JRASERVER-28519 citation added at the binding). A completion verifier applying AC4 literally ('either MEASURED... or explicitly marked UNVERIFIED') will reject the planned provenance-citation approach because it is neither a measurement nor an UNVERIFIED annotation. This is the bypass-annotation AC-contradiction pattern: the child plans to satisfy the criterion via a path the criterion text doesn't name.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend 79d5 AC4 to read: '... or documented at the binding with a primary-source citation (property name + canonical JRASERVER/JRACLOUD reference) recorded on this ticket — so a reader cannot mistake an assumption for a decision.' This makes the planned resolution formally acceptable without changing the intent.

findings.finding: The AC bullet 'no assertion added under this epic claims parity where the two adapters CORRECTLY diverge' is a negative-property constraint with no stated deterministic check; it cannot be evaluated in-session via a repo artifact or CI command.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — 'no assertion...claims parity where adapters CORRECTLY diverge' bullet
